title: The constructible topology of a spectral space is Hausdorff
statement: Let $X$ be a spectral space [def-weil-spectral-space]. Then the set $X$ endowed with its constructible topology [def-weil-pbc-constructible-topology] (the topology with subbase the quasi-compact open subsets of $X$ and their complements) is Hausdorff: for any two points $x\ne y$ of $X$ there are disjoint subsets $A,B\subseteq X$, both open in the constructible topology, with $x\in A$ and $y\in B$.

source.place: Topology, Lemma Tag 0901 (label lemma-constructible-hausdorff-quasi-compact, line 4305), the Hausdorff part (first paragraph of the proof)

proof.text:
*Step 1 (an open set separating $x$ and $y$).* Let $x

The singleton $\{x\}$ is irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components] (it is nonempty, and if $\{x\}=Z_1\cup Z_2$ with $Z_1,Z_2$ closed in $\{x\}$ then one of them contains $x$ and equals $\{x\}$), so its closure $\overline{\{x\}}$ is an irreducible closed subset of $X$ [lem-weil-pbc-irreducible-closure], and likewise $\overline{\{y\}}$. Suppose $x\in\overline{\{y\}}$ and $y\in\overline{\{x\}}$. Then $\overline{\{x\}}\subseteq\overline{\{y\}}$ and $\overline{\{y\}}\subseteq\overline{\{x\}}$, so $Z=\overline{\{x\}}=\overline{\{y\}}$ is an irreducible closed subset with the two generic points $x$ and $y$, and uniqueness gives $x=y$, a contradiction. source.place: Topology, Lemma Tag 0901 (lemma-constructible-hausdorff-quasi-compact, line 4305), proof, first paragraph

proof.text: *Step 2 (a quasi-compact open).* The quasi-compact open subsets of $X$ form a basis of its topology [def-weil-spectral-space], so there is a quasi-compact open $U\subseteq X$ with $x\in U\subseteq U_0$; since $y\notin U_0$, also $y\notin U$, i.e. $y\in X\setminus U$.

source.place: Topology, Lemma Tag 0901 (lemma-constructible-hausdorff-quasi-compact, line 4305), proof, first paragraph

proof.text: *Step 3 (conclusion).* $U$ is a quasi-compact open subset of $X$, so $U$ and $X\setminus U$ both belong to the subbase of the constructible topology [def-weil-pbc-constructible-topology] and are therefore open in it. Put $A=U$ and $B=X\setminus U$ (with the roles of $A$ and $B$ exchanged if $x$ and $y$ were renamed in Step 1). Then $A$ and $B$ are open in the constructible topology, $A\cap B=\emptyset$, $x\in A$ and $y\in B$. As $x\ne y$ were arbitrary, $X$ with its constructible topology is Hausdorff.
